In a standard left lateral view, the patient's left side is against the detector (image receptor), and the right side is closer to the X-ray source. - Actually, the rule is: On a lateral view, the right hemidiaphragm is usually visible anteriorly up to the anterior chest wall, while the left hemidiaphragm is visible posteriorly but fades out anteriorly behind the heart.
